text: With the Patriots preparing to host the Steelers at Gillette Stadium this Sunday, September 20 at 1 PM ET for their 2026 home opener, the big question looming over New England is whether Drake Maye and company can bounce back—and they'll have to do it without wide receiver A.J. Brown, who suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 1 and is headed to injured reserve for at least four games, leaving the receiving corps scrambling for answers about who steps up in his absence. On the roster front, the team re-signed safety Elliott Davison to the practice squad while releasing tight end Shane Zylstra, continuing their ongoing adjustments. Off the field, owner Robert Kraft made headlines by confirming he had rapper Macklemore removed as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's upcoming shows at Gillette Stadium, citing concerns about what Kraft described as "a history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community." Meanwhile, the Kraft family and Patriots Foundation continued their community work, donating $275,000 in the names of this year's Myra Kraft Community MVP Award winners, while quarterback Drake Maye and his wife Ann Michael demonstrated their own commitment to giving back by purchasing Amazon classroom wish lists for over 50 teachers and support specialists at Alfred Lima Sr. Elementary School
